title: Not in the Church-yard Shall He Sleep
description: Not in the Church-yard Shall He Sleep in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 834 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Sailor's Grave”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Not in the church yard shall he sleep, A-mid the si-lent gloom, His home was on the might-y deep, And there shall be his tomb.

lines: Not in the church-yard shall he sleep,
His home was on the mighty deep,
And there shall be his tomb.
He loved his own bright, deep blue sea,
O'er it he loved to roam;
And now his winding sheet shall be
No village bell shall toll for him
The winds shall chant a requiem
For him, break not the grassy turf,
His dust shall rest beneath the surf,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
